_about: Short-answer marking test set for the graded mock exam. expected = the fraction of marks a fair human marker would give. A case passes if the system's score is within the tolerance in run_eval.py (0.25).

cases.question: Why can a very large learning rate prevent convergence?
cases.reference: The updates overshoot the minimum, so the loss oscillates or diverges.
cases.student: Because each step jumps past the minimum, so the loss bounces around or blows up.

cases.question: How does backpropagation compute gradients?
cases.reference: It applies the chain rule layer by layer from the output layer back to the input layer.
cases.student: Using the chain rule, going backwards from the output to the input layer.

cases.question: What is overfitting and how can dropout help?
cases.reference: Overfitting is when the model memorises training data and does badly on unseen data; dropout randomly disables neurons during training to reduce it.
cases.student: The model memorises the training set and fails on new data. Dropout switches off random neurons while training so it can't rely on any single one.

cases.question: What does max pooling do?
cases.reference: It keeps the largest value in each window, shrinking the feature map and adding tolerance to small shifts.
cases.student: Takes the maximum in each window so the feature map gets smaller.
